name: France
summary: Major continental economic powerhouse with global leadership in aerospace, luxury goods, software, and low-carbon nuclear energy.

studentInfo.visaSummary: The VLS-TS student visa allows international students to work up to 60% of the annual working hours (964 hours/year).
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: Post-master's RECE authorization allows 12 to 24 months to find employment or launch a business.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Differentiated fees for non-EU students at public universities, with many exemptions and scholarships available.

name: Germany
summary: Europe's largest industrial economy, renowned for automotive engineering, advanced manufacturing, Mittelstand innovation, and software platforms.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Student residence permits allow working up to 140 full days or 280 half days per calendar year.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: 18-month post-study job seeker residence permit for university graduates.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Tuition-free at most public universities, with modest semester contribution fees.

name: Netherlands
summary: Global gateway to Europe, excelling in deep tech semiconductors, international logistics, agritech, and high-density commercial operations.

studentInfo.visaSummary: International students can work up to 16 hours per week with a relevant work permit arranged by the employer.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: 1-year Zoekjaar (Orientation Year) permit to seek employment as a highly skilled migrant.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Statutory tuition fees apply to EU/EEA students; institutional fees apply to non-EU students.

name: Italy
summary: Manufacturing cornerstone of southern Europe, leading in luxury design, industrial robotics, precision machinery, and aerospace systems.

studentInfo.visaSummary: International students holding a residence permit can work up to 20 hours per week (1,040 hours/year).
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: Up to 12 months permit for job search or business launch for Master's and PhD graduates.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Public university tuition is means-tested based on ISEE economic family indicators.

name: Sweden
summary: Nordic innovation frontrunner with world-class ecosystems in digital streaming, telecommunications, heavy commercial vehicles, and green industrial transition.

studentInfo.visaSummary: No official legal limit on student working hours, provided studies remain the primary activity.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: Up to 12 months residence permit extension to seek employment or explore starting a business.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Tuition is free for citizens of EU/EEA and Switzerland; fees apply for non-EU students.

name: Spain
summary: Dynamic southern European hub with rapid expansion in renewable energy, biotechnology, tourism infrastructure, and digital engineering hubs.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Student visa holders are permitted to work up to 30 hours per week under current immigration regulations.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: 12-month job seeker residence permit following graduation from higher education.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Public university credits vary by region, remaining highly competitive within Europe.

name: Switzerland
summary: Precision engineering and pharmaceutical heartland with top-tier research institutes, banking excellence, and cross-border commercial ties.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Non-EU students can work up to 15 hours per week after completing their first six months of residence.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: 6-month residence permit extension for graduates to find skilled work.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Federal institutes of technology offer exceptionally high academic value with moderate tuition fees.

name: Ireland
summary: English-speaking European digital and financial services hub hosting European headquarters for global software, cloud, and life sciences corporations.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Stamp 2 permission allows international students to work 20 hours per week during term time and 40 during holidays.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: Third Level Graduate Scheme provides up to 24 months post-study work for Master's degree holders.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Non-EU fee schedules set by individual universities, with strong scholarship availability.

name: Belgium
summary: Administrative and political capital of the European Union, featuring advanced petrochemicals, biopharma clusters, and semiconductor nanotechnology research.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Student residence permit allows up to 20 hours of work per week during the academic year.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: 12-month search year permit available to find a job or set up a business.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Tuition fees depend on region (Flanders vs Wallonia-Brussels) and student residency status.

name: Denmark
summary: Pioneer in offshore wind power, green maritime shipping, industrial enzyme synthesis, and sustainable urban design.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Non-EU students are allowed to work up to 20 hours a week and full-time in June, July and August.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: Up to 3-year establishment card granted automatically to graduates of Danish Master's programmes.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Higher education is free for EU/EEA citizens; annual fees apply to non-EU students.

name: Finland
summary: Nordic technology leader renowned for telecommunications infrastructure, clean technology, cyber security, and world-class educational rigor.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Students are permitted to work up to 30 hours per week on average during term time.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: Graduates can apply for an extended residence permit of up to 2 years to look for work or start a business.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Tuition fees apply to non-EU/EEA students studying in English-taught degree programmes.

name: Austria
summary: Central European hub linking Western and Eastern markets, excelling in automotive supply chains, industrial machinery, and environmental technology.

studentInfo.visaSummary: International students can work up to 20 hours per week with an employment permit.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: Graduates can extend their residence permit for 12 months to search for employment matching their qualifications.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Low fees for EU citizens; reasonable fixed rates for non-EU students at public universities.

name: Norway
summary: Pioneering energy transition leader with sovereign wealth capital, deep sea marine technology, carbon capture engineering, and electrification systems.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Study permits generally allow students to work part-time up to 20 hours per week during semester terms.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: Up to 1-year residence permit to look for work as a skilled worker after university completion.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Tuition fees apply to students from outside the EU/EEA and Switzerland at state universities.

name: Portugal
summary: Fast-growing southwestern tech hub hosting major tech summits, thriving remote worker infrastructure, and competitive software engineering talent.

studentInfo.visaSummary: Higher education students can work in Portugal with notification to the immigration authorities.
studentInfo.postStudyWorkDuration: 1-year temporary residence permit extension to find employment or launch an enterprise.
studentInfo.tuitionNotes: Public universities offer affordable tuition fees compared to northern and western European institutions.
